answer: Each identity locks 90 credits in a glacier register and files a work record bound to its key as one vertex. Any auditor may recompute hashes over six epochs and group near-identical records into a cluster. A proven cluster of size k makes each member forfeit its ferrous bond plus 20 credits per other member, so the k-th copy pays 90+20(k-1). A 1,000-copy cluster forfeits 20,070,000 credits; an honest identity pays 90 once and recovers it after a clean period. A rented record fails: its key mismatches the renter's history; a replayed hash is rejected as already filed.
